The initiative provides an independent data source confirming a broad decline in federal research support, which the research office can use to monitor and anticipate funding risks.

The outcome could set a significant precedent for federal research funding and higher education institutions broadly.

nih-grant-terminations.summary: Since mid-2026, NIH under Director Bhattacharya and the Trump administration has terminated numerous grants, including health disparities and other research, disrupting 1 in 30 clinical trials and affecting over 74,000 participants, while new funding policies and spending delays sharply lowered award odds. Senators McCormick and Fetterman have questioned the termination of more than 150 grants, and analyses show NIH funding has been substantially reshaped. As of early October 2026, the FY 2026 budget has been spent but significant uncertainty remains for researchers.

nsf-grant-decline.summary: Beginning in August 2026, reports indicated NSF was poised to issue its lowest number of new grants in four decades, falling over a billion dollars behind on expected awards. This represents a severe contraction in federal research support that directly threatens university grant pipelines.

white-house-pocket-rescission.summary: In late September 2026, the White House moved to block $810 million in congressionally approved funds through a pocket rescission, cancelling money for health, education, and international education programs, including $28 million from AHRQ. In early October, the GAO determined that OMB violated the Impoundment Control Act of 1974 and that HHS illegally withheld $78 million in health-care improvement agency funds. This raises questions for affected research areas—such as infection prevention—and signals a contested legal standoff over the executive branch's authority to withhold appropriated funding.
